provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Exercise every day
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate simple exercises.
The pupils should be able to explain why exercise is important.
Introduction:
We have learned about our body parts.
Today we will learn about keeping our body strong.
Content:
Exercise means moving our body.
Running makes our legs strong.
Skipping makes our heart happy.
Stretching helps us bend and reach.
We exercise every morning in school.
Class activity:
Let us form a circle and do morning exercises.
Run in place, skip rope and stretch high.
Evaluation questions:
What is exercise?
Show me how to run.
Why do we exercise?
Summary:
Exercise every day to keep our body strong and healthy.

topics.title: Safety on the stairs
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state how to walk safely on stairs.
The pupils should be able to identify unsafe behaviors on stairs.
Introduction:
We use stairs to go up and down.
Some children get hurt on stairs.
Content:
Always hold the rail when climbing stairs.
Walk one step at a time.
Do not run or play on stairs.
Do not push others on stairs.
Stairs are not for jumping or climbing.
Class activity:
Let us practice walking up and down stairs safely.
Hold the rail and take slow steps.
Evaluation questions:
What should we hold on stairs?
Should we run on stairs?
Show me how to walk safely.
Summary:
Hold the rail and walk carefully to stay safe on stairs.

topics.title: Playground safety
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list playground safety rules.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate taking turns on equipment.
Introduction:
The playground is fun for playing.
We must play safely to avoid accidents.
Content:
Take turns when using the slide.
Do not push others on swings.
Sand stays low, not in eyes or mouth.
Check the ground for sharp things.
Wear shoes to protect your feet.
Class activity:
Let us practice taking turns on the slide.
We will line up and wait for our turn.
Evaluation questions:
What rule should we follow on the slide?
Show me how to take turns.
Why should we wear shoes on playground?
Summary:
Play safely and take turns to keep the playground fun for everyone.

topics.title: Sun safety
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify sun protection items.
The pupils should be able to explain why we need shade in hot sun.
Introduction:
The sun is very hot in Nigeria.
Too much sun can hurt our skin.
Content:
Stay in shade when the sun is hot.
Drink plenty of water to stay cool.
Wear a cap to protect your head.
Use umbrella when walking outside.
Wear light clothes to stay cool.
Class activity:
Let us play a game of finding shade.
When I say sun, find shade quickly.
Evaluation questions:
What should we wear in hot sun?
Where should we stay when sun is hot?
Show me how to drink water properly.
Summary:
Use shade, water and a cap to stay safe in the hot sun.

topics.title: Rainy day safety
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list rain safety items.
The pupils should be able to explain why flood water is dangerous.
Introduction:
Rain comes during harmattan season.
Rain can make some places slippery and dangerous.
Content:
Wear boots to keep feet dry.
Wear raincoat to stay dry.
Do not wade in flood water.
Flood water may have germs or sharp things.
Walk carefully on wet ground.
Class activity:
Let us practice putting on raincoat and boots.
We will pretend it is raining outside.
Evaluation questions:
What do we wear when it rains?
Should we play in flood water?
Show me how to walk on wet ground.
Summary:
Wear rain gear and avoid flood water to stay safe on rainy days.

topics.title: Insects and bites
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify dangerous insects.
The pupils should be able to explain what to do when bitten.
Introduction:
Many insects live around us.
Some insects can bite and hurt us.
Content:
Do not disturb bees or wasps.
Do not touch ants or spiders.\Tell a teacher if an insect bites you.
Do not scratch insect bites.
Wash bites with soap and water.
Class activity:
Let us play a game of spotting insects.
When you see a picture of a bee, say 'danger'.
Evaluation questions:
Which insects should we not touch?
What should we do if bitten by an insect?
Show me how to tell a teacher about bites.
Summary:
Stay away from insects and tell adults about bites to stay safe.

topics.title: Wounds and first help
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate cleaning a small cut.
The pupils should be able to identify when to tell an adult about a wound.
Introduction:\Sometimes we get small cuts or scrapes.
We need to know how to help ourselves.
Content:
Tell an adult when you bleed.
Wash small cuts with clean water.
Cover cuts with a plaster.
Do not touch dirty wounds.
Let adults help big wounds.
Class activity:
Let us practice cleaning a pretend cut.
We will use water and a clean cloth.
Evaluation questions:
What should we do when we bleed?
Show me how to wash a small cut.
When should we tell an adult about wounds?
Summary:
Wash and cover small cuts and tell adults about big wounds.

topics.title: Sickness and rest
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list signs of being sick.
The pupils should be able to explain why rest is important when sick.
Introduction:
Sometimes we feel sick and cannot come to school.
Our body needs rest to get better.
Content:
Rest when you have fever or headache.
Stay in bed until you feel better.
Take medicine only from adults.
Drink water when you are sick.
Tell your parents how you feel.
Class activity:
Let us pretend to be sick and take rest.
We will lie down quietly and imagine getting better.
Evaluation questions:
What should we do when we are sick?
Should we take medicine alone?
Show me how to rest properly.
Summary:
Rest and take medicine only from adults to get well soon.

topics.title: Clinic visit
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state what happens at the clinic.
The pupils should be able to explain why we should not fear the clinic.
Introduction:
Sometimes we need to visit the clinic.
The nurse helps us stay healthy.
Content:
The nurse checks our height and weight.
The nurse checks our eyes and ears.
The nurse gives us medicine if needed.
The nurse asks how we feel.
Do not be afraid of the clinic.
Class activity:
Let us play a game of visiting the clinic.
We will take turns being the nurse and patient.
Evaluation questions:
What does the nurse check at the clinic?
Should we be afraid of the clinic?
Show me how to answer the nurse's questions.
Summary:
The nurse helps us stay healthy so we should not fear the clinic.

topics.title: Revision and safety patrol
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify unsafe situations.
The pupils should be able to recall safety rules learned.
Introduction:
We have learned many safety rules.
Today we will practice what we know.
Content:
Look at pictures and spot unsafe things.\Remember to hold the rail on stairs.
Take turns on playground equipment.
Use shade and water in hot sun.
Wear boots in rainy weather.
Class activity:
Let us play safety patrol.
We will walk around the room and point out unsafe things.
Evaluation questions:
Show me an unsafe picture and explain why.
What safety rule do you remember most?
How do we stay safe on stairs?
Summary:
Remember all safety rules to keep yourself and others safe.
